\begin{quote}
\textbf{Augmented Competition:} Consider two firms playing a two-stage game with discount factor \(\delta\). In the first stage they play a Cournot quantity-setting game in which each firm has costs \(c_i(q_i) = 10q_i\) for \(i \in \{1, 2\}\) and the demand is given by \(p(q) = 100 - q\), where \(q = q_1 + q_2\). In the second stage, after the results of the Cournot game are observed, the firms play the following standard-setting game:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}ccc@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Player 1 ~Player 2 & \(a\) & \(b\) \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\(A\) & 100, 100 & 0, 0 \\
\(B\) & 0, 0 & 300, 300 \\
\end{longtable}
}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Find the unique Nash equilibrium of the first-stage game and the two pure-strategy Nash equilibria of the second-stage game.
\item
  As far as the two firms are considered, what are the symmetric Pareto-optimal outcomes of each stage-game?
\item
  For which values of \(\delta\) can the Pareto-optimal outcomes be supported as a subgame-perfect equilibrium?
\item
  Assume that \(\delta = 0.5\). What is the ``best'' symmetric subgame-perfect equilibrium that the players can support?
\item
  What happens to the best symmetric subgame-perfect equilibrium that the players can support as \(\delta\) drops toward zero?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
